subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw add a caller-readable inter-session run-progress API for `sessions_send`, and should the product shape be a new `sessions_subscribe` tool, an `agent.events` gateway RPC, or a `sessions_send` progress option?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the permanent API crosses session authorization, event replay, redaction, retention, and channel-delivery boundaries that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Design a bounded subscribe API
options.body: Approve a `sessions_subscribe`/`agent.events`-style contract with explicit observer authorization, bounded replay, redaction, retention, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold progress into sessions_send
options.body: Add an explicit progress option to `sessions_send`, preserving current default behavior while documenting blocking and delivery semantics.

options.title: Defer to structured process events
options.body: Keep this issue open but make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/52826 the prerequisite for the canonical progress taxonomy before adding a sessions-specific tool.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded subscribe API
recommendation.body: Approve a `sessions_subscribe`/`agent.events`-style contract with explicit observer authorization, bounded replay, redaction, retention, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest available current-main blame signal across the central sessions and gateway event surfaces touched by the decision.
